quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: The center of a traffic lane usually has an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride on the left or right side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could make the bike tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could make the bike tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the U-turn.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist usually ride in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: When it starts raining, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track usually works best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Practice is the best way to learn.
Just start riding. All bikes are similar.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, check safety and maintenance items. Find where everything is located. Then practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how the bike shifts gears.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Stop the engine power from changing in the middle of the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Stop the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the engine power from changing in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting during a turn can suddenly change power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:

options.text: Not enough oil.
Not enough fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: An engine seizes when it runs low on oil. Without oil, the moving parts cannot slide smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain starts, the road becomes slippery. Rainwater mixes with oil left by cars on the pavement. Riding in tire tracks left by other cars gives you better grip.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Your BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold onto the operator's waist or hips. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Wait.
Drink coffee.
Exercise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to wait. Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What gloves should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Wear half-fingered gloves.
Wear full-fingered gloves.
Not wear gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear full-fingered gloves made of durable material. They improve your grip and protect your hands.

questions.question: Which is NOT a method to control a motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Accelerate through the turn.
Reduce your speed before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before entering the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean into the turn and roll on the throttle to stabilize the suspension.

questions.question: What should you wear while riding to protect your hearing?

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from long-term exposure to engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from long-term exposure to engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time. Even a full-face helmet does not fully protect your hearing. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: What about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding unless it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Should be consistently checked by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be consistently checked by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular habit.
